notes.text: Since 1 January 2019 the National Bank of Romania has capped total debt service at 40% of a household's net income, raised by 5 percentage points for first-time home buyers, with up to 15% of new loans exempt. When the limit was set, the median DSTI on new mortgages for borrowers below the median wage was 50%, so the cap binds mainly on lower-income buyers and limits how far credit can lift prices at the entry level.

notes.text: Romania differentiated LTV limits by currency from 2011 and, since 2019, caps debt service on unhedged foreign-currency loans at 20% of income against 40% for lei loans, policies the National Bank designed to steer new mortgage credit into domestic currency. As a result, mortgage costs depend chiefly on domestic lei rates set by National Bank of Romania policy more than on euro area rates.

notes.text: The state-guaranteed Noua Casa programme, run by FNGCIMM, lets buyers with no home, or one under 50 square metres, buy with a 5% down payment on loans up to EUR 66,500 with a guarantee of up to 50%, or 15% down on new homes with loans up to EUR 119,000 and a guarantee of up to 60%. The guarantee ceiling for 2026 is RON 500 million, so the scheme sustains entry-level and new-build demand within a capped annual envelope.

notes.text: The National Institute of Statistics compiles Romania's house price index quarterly from transaction prices recorded by public notaries, covering household purchases nationwide with separate new and existing dwelling sub-indices, and existing homes split into Bucharest and other apartments and urban and rural houses. It uses hedonic rolling time-dummy models and is published about 112 days after the quarter ends, so it lags faster market indicators.
